messages:
sara (AE): FYI Seastack POC run this morning showed weird tail jitter at QPS ~450. forwarding raw logs and question: is this normal for their workload or something we need to change in the plan?

josh (SE): can you paste the exact load command and model+sequence settings?

sara (AE): load command they ran: `heyload --target https://api.redwood.ai/generate --concurrency 200 --qps 450 --duration 15m --prompt-file seastack_prompts.txt`

sara (AE): model: rdx-7b-quant, max_tokens=256, avg_prompt_tokens~40, tail events are 99p latency spikes up to 2.6s (baseline ~220ms)

josh (SE): thanks. couple quick checks: were they using Dedicated pool or Hosted fallback? and did they enable prefix caching?

sara (AE): Dedicated pool (reserved), single region us-west-2. they said caching was off in their harness to avoid stateful artifacts.

leo (SRE): saw the logs Sara dropped. notable pattern: spikes correlate with short microbursts (50–100ms) where concurrent requests exceed batch window and fallback to sync path. also a few GC-ish stalls on a node around minute 7.

leo (SRE): quick mitigation suggestions: 1) enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts 2) set `batch_timeout_ms` to 6–8ms (we default 12) to reduce sync fallbacks 3) pin to a slightly larger instance SKU for headroom (one extra GPU slot)

josh (SE): agree. also recommend trying `--qps 420` steady Poisson (not fixed inter-arrival) to emulate realistic variance. and test with our stress harness that replays token counts instead of average token size.

sara (AE): noted. They also asked about pricing if we recommend bumping Dedicated pool size for headroom.

alina (Pricing): rough numbers: bumping from 4 -> 5 GPU reserved pool adds ~$11k/mo on top of current commit. if they prefer burst, we can enable burst capacity which charges at higher unit rate but no commit. i can run detailed delta with their expected 24/7 baseline vs peak hours if you share utilization profile.

sara (AE): I have their 24h tail profile — will DM. question: any blocking security concerns with enabling KV caching for PII prompts? Seastack asked about that.

leo (SRE): KV/prefix caching stores short-lived keys in ephemeral instance memory by default. for regulated PII use we recommend either client-side redaction or switching to Private deployment with customer-managed KMS. caching itself can be disabled per-route. not a blocker but we should document options for the SOC questionnaire.

josh (SE): I'll prepare a minimal test matrix: (A) keep current config but reduce batch_timeout, (B) enable prefix caching + reduced timeout, (C) add one GPU to pool + B. will run each for 20m steady Poisson and attach 99/99.9p numbers.

sara (AE): timeline? the customer wants results before their Friday exec sync.

josh (SE): I can spin tests Wed morning and have a writeup by Thu EOD.

alina (Pricing): I can draft a one-pager with committed vs burst cost and SLA delta by Thu noon if Josh shares expected extra GPU hours.

devops-bot: deployment noted: `canary/dedicated/us-west-2` config update scheduled at 03:10 UTC to apply `batch_timeout_ms=8` to test pool

leo (SRE): once canary runs, I'll watch node metrics and GC logs. if spikes persist, we'll try the larger SKU.

sara (AE): perfect — thanks team. I'll update the Seastack contact and block the Fri exec slot pending results. :thumbsup:

josh (SE): ping me in thread when canary starts so I can tail the harness logs.

sara (AE): will do.
